summary: Defines the architecture of IPFIX, a way for network devices to watch traffic flows and send summaries of them to a collecting system. It describes the roles of the devices that measure and export flow data and the collector that receives it. It is an informational overview rather than the protocol itself.

plainLanguage.summary: Imagine a road counter that notes how many cars drive past and where they go, then mails a tally to a central office. This note explains how those counters and the office fit together.

questions: how does ip flow export architecture work
subtitle: The blueprint for measuring network traffic as flows and exporting the results to a collector.

tldr.problem: Accounting, traffic engineering, intrusion detection and QoS monitoring all need flow-based traffic measurements, and there was no standard way to export them.
tldr.mechanism: The architecture splits the job into observation points, metering processes that build Flow Records, an exporting process that sends them in IPFIX Messages, and a collecting process that decodes them using Templates.
tldr.outcome: It is an overview that sets requirements for recovery and security and points to RFC 5101 and RFC 5102 for the protocol and information model. It was later updated by RFC 6183.

today: RFC 5470 is an Informational RFC published in March 2009 and has been updated by RFC 6183. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
Usage-based accounting, traffic profiling, traffic engineering, attack and intrusion detection, and quality-of-service monitoring all need flow-based IP traffic measurements. This memo defines the architecture for IP Flow Information eXport (IPFIX): the key components (at least IPFIX Devices and Collectors), the architectural requirements such as recovery and security, and the characteristics of the protocol.

The work is split across several documents. RFC 3917 gives the requirements, RFC 5101 specifies the protocol, RFC 5102 the information model and RFC 5472 the applicability. IPFIX does not provide remote configuration of a device; implementors must supply their own way.
sections.plainLanguage: Many jobs need to know what kinds of traffic cross a network. This paper draws the plan for how counting devices report to a central collector.

sections.title: Flows, Keys and Records
sections.content:
A Flow is a set of IP packets passing an Observation Point during a certain time interval, all sharing a set of common properties. A property comes from packet header fields, characteristics of the packet itself (such as the number of MPLS labels), or packet treatment (such as the output interface). Each field used to define a Flow is a Flow Key.

A Flow Record holds measured properties (such as total bytes) and usually characteristic properties (such as source address) of one Flow. The memo's examples show that masking address bits merges Flows, so eight Flows can become six, and that a filter fixing key values can reduce those to one.

An Observation Point is a place where packets can be seen, such as a single router port. An Observation Domain is the largest set of Observation Points whose Flow information a Metering Process can aggregate, and it carries an Observation Domain ID.
sections.plainLanguage: A flow is a group of cars that share something, like the same start and end. A record is the tally sheet for one such group.

sections.title: The Functional Blocks
sections.content:
An IPFIX Device hosts at least one Exporting Process and may have many Observation Points and Metering Processes. The Metering Process captures packet headers, timestamps them, applies optional sampling and filtering, classifies packets into Flows and maintains Flow Records. A Flow expires when no packets are seen for a configurable time (a zero timeout reports single-packet Flows), when resources run short, or on a regular schedule for long-running Flows.

The Exporting Process decides when and whether to export expired Flows and sends them to one or more Collectors. The Collecting Process uses each Flow Record's Template ID to interpret its Information Elements, and must accept and decode IPFIX Messages from different Exporting Process and Observation Domain pairs, and store the Control Information and Flow Records.

Packet selection may use sampling functions (for example every 100th packet, with 1:1 meaning no sampling) and filter functions, such as Protocol == TCP, Destination Port < 1024. The memo recommends selecting packets after checksums have been verified.
sections.plainLanguage: One part watches and counts, one part packs the tallies into envelopes and sends them, and one part opens the envelopes at the office.

sections.title: Control Information and Export
sections.content:
IPFIX exports two kinds of information. Control Information includes the Flow definition, selection criteria and Templates that describe the data. The Data Stream carries the Flow Records. A Template is an ordered sequence of type and length pairs identified by a Template ID. Templates let new fields be added without changing the record format, let a Collector skip fields it does not understand, and allow exporting only the fields required.

Control Information should reach the Collector before the Flow Records it describes and should travel reliably. A device must use a congestion-aware transport. If the network is not reliable, at least Control Information should use reliable transport, while the Data Stream may use either. The memo names SCTP, TCP and UDP. UDP is unreliable only, so operators would need to keep traffic within their own administrative domains, for example on a dedicated network.

When metering falls short of resources, the device should count and report packet losses to its Collectors.
sections.plainLanguage: Before sending tallies, the counter first sends a legend that says what each column means. Without it the office could not read the numbers.

sections.title: Collector Failure and Redundancy
sections.content:
The transport connection is pre-configured between the device and the Collector. The device should set a keepalive (such as the TCP keepalive timeout or the SCTP HEARTBEAT interval) low enough to detect a Collector failure quickly. Extremely short intervals can wrongly abort the connection during transient congestion and add load.

With a single Collector, the device should stop sending Flow Records on a keepalive timeout and try to reconnect. With secondary Collectors, it opens a Data Stream to the one of next highest priority, sending Control Information too if the session was not opened in advance. Redundant Collectors can instead receive all streams at once. Because IPFIX requires a congestion-aware transport, multicast is not an option for redundancy.

The memo also flags special cases, such as tunnels, VPNs, firewalls that drop packets and NAT devices that change Flow Key values, and says guidelines are needed for classifying such traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: If the office stops answering, the counter notices, stops mailing, and can switch to a backup office on its list.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
An IPFIX system must provide different levels of protection on the wire. Three levels should be supported: host-based security (none, when the transport is perceived as safe, which a system must support), authentication-only (integrity and authenticity but no confidentiality, with replay protection) and encryption (required when the transport is unsafe). The memo recommends using TLS or DTLS where they satisfy the need.

End-point authentication should let either one-way or mutual authentication happen between device and Collector. Overload may lose data, so Collectors should detect lost Flow Records and at least record how many. IPFIX-specific attacks include spoofed export packets, and encrypting control packets both ways helps a Collector ignore spoofed data.
sections.plainLanguage: You can send the tallies in a plain envelope, a sealed one, or a locked box. You pick based on how much you trust the road between.

items.title: Metering Process
items.text: Observes packets at an Observation Point and builds Flow Records.

items.title: Exporting Process
items.text: Sends Flow Records and Templates to one or more Collectors.

items.title: Collecting Process
items.text: Receives Flow Records and uses Templates to decode them.
